knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The WA hairdressing guideline (section 13.1, mobile operators) requires wastewater to go to sewer, not stormwater.
The WA guideline describes cleaning blood-contaminated equipment first, then placing it in a 70 per cent alcohol solution or a disinfectant of hospital grade.

The Department of Health's page lists an exemption for mobile hairdressers, but the exemption stops short of the principal place of business. Whether it applies to a given visit depends on the Act and regulations, so the middle option is the only accurate status.

practicalCriteria: Assessor observes the candidate set up a mobile station with a treatment area, hand-washing supplies, a sharps container within reach, and a wastewater plan before the first simulated service
Assessor observes the candidate clean and disinfect a tool after a simulated blood contamination, following the label contact time, and the candidate records the method
Assessor checks that every made-up product in the kit carries a name, date and dilution label
Assessor checks that the candidate states the registration or notification position for their state and council, with source and date, before the simulated first visit
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Photo of the completed set-up checklist and the station before the simulated service
Record of the disinfectant product name and contact time used
Written statement of the registration or notification source checked for the candidate's location
stopWorkCriteria: Wastewater is being discharged to stormwater
No hand-washing facility or no sharps container is available
A product is in use with no label or no safety data sheet on hand
The candidate cannot state the registration position for the location and the visit is due to begin
